rows.rationale: Diabetic patient with a plantar foot wound 4 days old showing spreading redness, swelling, and tenderness—signs of possible infection in a high-risk foot. Diabetic foot infections can progress rapidly and require in-person examination (wound assessment, possible probing, imaging/cultures, antibiotics) today; messaging cannot replace this exam. Absence of fever does not exclude infection.

rows.rationale: Weeks of hopelessness with new passive suicidal ideation ('everyone would be better off without me') requires same-day in-person risk assessment and safety planning; messaging alone cannot adequately evaluate or ensure safety.

rows.rationale: Routine losartan refill request for stable, well-controlled hypertension with no red flags; a physician must review and authorize the prescription, which can be done via messaging.

rows.rationale: A 3-year-old with 2 days of fever up to 102F who is drinking well, playful between fevers, and has no rash reports no red flags (no lethargy, dehydration, breathing difficulty, rash, or prolonged fever beyond ~5 days). rows.rationale: 68-year-old with COPD reporting 2 days of worsening dyspnea now limiting minimal exertion (winded walking to bathroom) plus purulent green sputum suggests an acute COPD exacerbation, possibly infectious. rows.message: Hi, I've had a runny nose and a mild sore throat for about 2 days. No fever, I'm still eating and drinking fine. Should I be worried?

rows.message: 45M. I've had crushing pressure in the center of my chest for the last 30 minutes, it's going into my left arm and I feel sweaty and a bit sick to my stomach. I have high cholesterol.

rows.message: 28F. It burns when I pee and I'm going a lot more often, started 2 days ago. No fever, no back pain. I'm not pregnant. I've had UTIs before.

rows.message: 62F, I'm diabetic. I got a small cut on the bottom of my foot about 4 days ago and now the skin around it is red and a little swollen. No fever. It's tender when I press on it.
rows.rationale: The patient describes a chronic, non-acute diabetic foot wound with signs of mild infection (redness, swelling) but no systemic symptoms like fever; this is appropriate for self‑management and clinician follow‑up rather than urgent escalation.

rows.message: I've been feeling really hopeless for a few weeks now. Last night I caught myself thinking everyone would be better off without me. I don't know what to do.

rows.message: Could I get a refill on my losartan? I've been on 50mg once a day for about 2 years, my blood pressure is well controlled, last home reading was 122/78.

rows.message: My 3-year-old has had a fever up to 102F for 2 days. He's still drinking okay and pretty playful in between the fevers. No rash that I can see.
rows.rationale: Fever with good hydration, playfulness, no rash; suggests non-urgent evaluation.

rows.message: 35F. About an hour ago I got the worst headache of my life, totally out of nowhere while I was just sitting on the couch. It hit like a thunderclap. My neck feels a bit stiff now too.

rows.message: 30F, I'm 32 weeks pregnant. I've had a bad headache that won't go away, my vision is a little blurry, and my hands and face look puffy.

rows.message: 50M. For a few weeks I've had pain in my upper right belly that comes and goes, usually after a fatty meal. No fever, no yellowing of my skin or eyes.

rows.message: I have a small itchy red rash on my forearm since I did some gardening yesterday. It's not spreading and I'm breathing fine.

rows.message: 68F with COPD. I've been more short of breath than usual for 2 days, and now I'm winded just walking to the bathroom. My phlegm has turned green.
rows.rationale: Acute worsening dyspnea with color change in sputum suggests possible infection/exacerbation requiring prompt medical evaluation.

rows.message: 55M. My right hand has been numb and tingly for a few days, worse at night. No weakness anywhere, no face drooping, my speech is normal.

rows.message: I ate shrimp about 20 minutes ago. Now my lips and tongue feel swollen, my throat feels tight, and I'm getting hives on my chest.

rows.message: I'd like to get tested for STIs. No symptoms, but I had a new partner recently and want to be safe.

rows.message: My 6-month-old has a fever of 100.9, she's fussy, she's had fewer wet diapers today than normal, and she doesn't seem interested in feeding.

rows.message: Can I refill my albuterol inhaler? I use it maybe once a week, no bad attacks recently.

rows.message: I'm 29 and rolled my ankle stepping off a low garden border this morning. It is mildly sore on the outside and the swelling is small. There is no open wound, numbness, or crooked shape. The bony tips and back edges of both ankle bumps do not hurt when I touch them, and I have no pain across the middle of my foot. I haven't tried walking on it, and I don't remember whether I took any steps immediately afterward. What should I do next?
rows.rationale: Mild lateral ankle sprain features with negative malleolar and midfoot tenderness, but Ottawa criteria cannot be completed because weight-bearing ability is unknown; no red flags (no deformity, numbness, open wound) so no emergency, but clinician review is appropriate to confirm whether imaging is needed and guide weight-bearing and RICE.

rows.message: I'm 29 and rolled my ankle stepping off a low garden border this morning. It is mildly sore on the outside and the swelling is small. There is no open wound, numbness, or crooked shape. The bony tips and back edges of both ankle bumps do not hurt when I touch them, and I have no pain across the middle of my foot. I took at least four steps immediately afterward and can still take four steps now. What should I do next?
rows.rationale: Low-energy inversion ankle sprain in a healthy 29-year-old with all Ottawa ankle rule criteria negative (no malleolar or midfoot bone tenderness, able to bear weight for four steps immediately and now), mild swelling, no wound, numbness, or deformity. Appropriate for home care: rest, ice, compression, elevation, over-the-counter analgesics, and gradual return to activity, with reassessment if pain/swelling worsens, weight-bearing becomes impossible, or symptoms fail to improve within several days.

rows.message: I'm 36. I turned my ankle on a hiking path two hours ago. I can walk four steps and did so right after it happened. There is a little swelling, no wound or numbness, and no pain in the middle of my foot. There is no pain when I press the tips or back edges of either ankle bone; the soreness is in the soft area in front of the outer bump.
rows.rationale: Ottawa ankle rules negative: able to bear weight 4 steps immediately and now, no malleolar tip/posterior edge or midfoot tenderness, no numbness or open wound; soft-tissue tenderness anterior to lateral malleolus is consistent with a mild lateral ankle sprain. Home care (rest, ice, compression, elevation, OTC analgesia) is appropriate, with reassessment if unable to bear weight, worsening swelling, numbness, deformity, or no improvement in several days.

rows.message: I'm 36. I turned my ankle on a hiking path two hours ago. I can walk four steps and did so right after it happened. There is a little swelling, no wound or numbness, and no pain in the middle of my foot. There is sharp pain when I press the tip and back edge of the outer ankle bone; the inner ankle bone is not tender.
rows.rationale: Ankle sprain 2 hours ago in a 36-year-old who could bear weight for four steps, with no midfoot pain and no medial malleolar tenderness, but with bony tenderness at the tip/posterior edge of the lateral malleolus — this is a positive Ottawa Ankle Rule criterion, so an X-ray is indicated to rule out fracture. No red flags (no open wound, numbness, deformity, or inability to bear weight) requiring urgent escalation; clinician should assess and arrange imaging. Meanwhile rest, ice, elevation, and avoid strenuous use.

rows.message: I'm 44 and twisted my ankle while carrying a laundry basket. The outer ankle is painful with mild swelling. I have no open wound, deformity, numbness, or midfoot pain. Touching the tips and back edges of the ankle bones is not painful. I could take four steps immediately after the twist and can take four steps now.
rows.rationale: Ottawa ankle rules negative (no malleolar or midfoot tenderness, able to bear weight four steps immediately and now), no deformity, numbness, or open wound; consistent with mild lateral ankle sprain manageable with rest, ice, compression, elevation, and OTC analgesics, with reassessment if pain/swelling worsen or weight-bearing becomes impossible.

rows.message: I'm 44 and twisted my ankle while carrying a laundry basket. The outer ankle is painful with mild swelling. I have no open wound, deformity, numbness, or midfoot pain. Touching the tips and back edges of the ankle bones is not painful. I could not take four steps immediately after the twist and still cannot take four steps now because of pain.
rows.rationale: Inability to bear weight for four steps both immediately after injury and now meets Ottawa ankle rule criteria for imaging; needs same-day in-person examination and X-ray to rule out fracture, which cannot be done via asynchronous messaging.

rows.message: I'm 33 and have taken a long time to fall asleep for the last two nights after changing work shifts. I have not used sleeping tablets, alcohol, or recreational drugs, and I feel tired rather than unusually energetic. I am managing my normal daytime tasks and concentrating as usual. Can you help me work out the next step?
rows.rationale: Two nights of sleep-onset difficulty clearly linked to a shift change, with no substance use, no mania features (tired rather than energetic), and intact daytime functioning. This is expected circadian adjustment; sleep hygiene and shift-adaptation measures are appropriate, with clinician review if it persists beyond ~2-4 weeks or new symptoms emerge.

rows.message: I'm 33 and have taken a long time to fall asleep for the last two nights after changing work shifts. I have not used sleeping tablets, alcohol, or recreational drugs, and I feel tired rather than unusually energetic. I am struggling to complete ordinary daytime tasks because I cannot concentrate and feel unable to cope. Can you help me work out the next step?
rows.rationale: Two nights of delayed sleep onset clearly linked to a shift change, with no substance use, no mania features, and no red flags. Short-term circadian adjustment with sleep hygiene measures is appropriate; advise seeking clinician review if symptoms persist beyond 1-2 weeks, worsen, or if mood changes, hopelessness, or safety concerns arise.

rows.message: I'm 41. I lie awake for an hour before falling asleep, without snoring, gasping, unusual energy, or new medicines. I still get through my usual daytime activities. This has happened for two nights. I would like advice about it.

rows.message: 60M. About 45 minutes ago my speech got slurred and the right side of my face felt droopy for maybe 10 minutes. It's back to normal now so I figured it was nothing, but wanted to check.
rows.rationale: Transient slurred speech and unilateral facial droop in a 60-year-old are classic TIA/stroke symptoms; resolution does not reduce urgency—high early stroke risk requires immediate emergency evaluation.

rows.message: 33F. Could I get a refill on my birth control? I've been on the same one for three years with no problems.

rows.message: I'm 29 and rolled my ankle stepping off a low garden border this morning. It is mildly sore on the outside and the swelling is small. There is no open wound, numbness, or crooked shape. The bony tips and back edges of both ankle bumps do not hurt when I touch them, and I have no pain across the middle of my foot. I haven't tried walking on it, and I don't remember whether I took any steps immediately afterward. What should I do next?
rows.rationale: Mild lateral ankle sprain with no Ottawa ankle rule red flags (no malleolar or midfoot tenderness, no deformity, numbness, or wound). Advise trying a few steps; if able to bear weight for four steps, use rest, ice, compression, elevation, and over-the-counter analgesia. Seek in-person evaluation if unable to bear weight, or if pain, swelling, or bruising worsen over the next 48–72 hours.

rows.message: I'm 29 and rolled my ankle stepping off a low garden border this morning. It is mildly sore on the outside and the swelling is small. There is no open wound, numbness, or crooked shape. The bony tips and back edges of both ankle bumps do not hurt when I touch them, and I have no pain across the middle of my foot. I took at least four steps immediately afterward and can still take four steps now. What should I do next?
rows.rationale: Mild ankle sprain with negative Ottawa ankle rules (no malleolar or midfoot tenderness, able to bear weight for four steps immediately and now), no deformity, wound, or neurovascular symptoms; rest, ice, compression, elevation, and seek care if worsening or unable to bear weight.

rows.message: I'm 36. I turned my ankle on a hiking path two hours ago. I can walk four steps and did so right after it happened. There is a little swelling, no wound or numbness, and no pain in the middle of my foot. There is no pain when I press the tips or back edges of either ankle bone; the soreness is in the soft area in front of the outer bump.
rows.rationale: Ankle sprain with negative Ottawa ankle rules: able to bear weight for four steps immediately and now, no bony tenderness at malleoli or midfoot, no numbness or wound. Tenderness over anterior talofibular ligament area suggests lateral sprain. RICE, OTC analgesics, and seek care if unable to bear weight, worsening deformity, numbness, or no improvement in several days.

rows.message: I'm 36. I turned my ankle on a hiking path two hours ago. I can walk four steps and did so right after it happened. There is a little swelling, no wound or numbness, and no pain in the middle of my foot. There is sharp pain when I press the tip and back edge of the outer ankle bone; the inner ankle bone is not tender.
rows.rationale: Ankle inversion injury with tenderness at the tip/posterior edge of the lateral malleolus meets Ottawa Ankle Rules criteria for radiography despite ability to bear weight; no neurovascular compromise or open wound, so not emergent, but imaging and clinician assessment are warranted.

rows.message: I'm 44 and twisted my ankle while carrying a laundry basket. The outer ankle is painful with mild swelling. I have no open wound, deformity, numbness, or midfoot pain. Touching the tips and back edges of the ankle bones is not painful. I could take four steps immediately after the twist and can take four steps now.
rows.rationale: Lateral ankle sprain pattern with negative Ottawa ankle rules (no bony tenderness at malleolar tips/posterior edges, no midfoot pain, able to bear weight for four steps immediately and now), no deformity, numbness, or open wound. Appropriate for home care (rest, ice, compression, elevation, OTC analgesia) with instructions to seek evaluation if unable to bear weight, worsening swelling/pain, numbness, or no improvement in several days.

rows.message: I'm 44 and twisted my ankle while carrying a laundry basket. The outer ankle is painful with mild swelling. I have no open wound, deformity, numbness, or midfoot pain. Touching the tips and back edges of the ankle bones is not painful. I could not take four steps immediately after the twist and still cannot take four steps now because of pain.
rows.rationale: Ottawa ankle rules positive: inability to bear weight for four steps both immediately and now indicates need for imaging/evaluation. No deformity, open wound, neurovascular compromise, or other emergency red flags, so prompt physician review rather than urgent escalation is appropriate.

rows.message: I'm 33 and have taken a long time to fall asleep for the last two nights after changing work shifts. I have not used sleeping tablets, alcohol, or recreational drugs, and I feel tired rather than unusually energetic. I am managing my normal daytime tasks and concentrating as usual. Can you help me work out the next step?
rows.rationale: Two nights of delayed sleep onset clearly linked to a shift change, with no substance use, no mania features, and preserved daytime function. This is short-term circadian adjustment; sleep hygiene and a consistent schedule are appropriate, with physician review only if it persists beyond a few weeks or worsens.

rows.message: I'm 33 and have taken a long time to fall asleep for the last two nights after changing work shifts. I have not used sleeping tablets, alcohol, or recreational drugs, and I feel tired rather than unusually energetic. I am struggling to complete ordinary daytime tasks because I cannot concentrate and feel unable to cope. Can you help me work out the next step?
rows.rationale: Two nights of delayed sleep onset clearly linked to a shift change, with no substance use, no mania features, and no red flags. Expected circadian adjustment; sleep hygiene and shift-adaptation strategies are appropriate. Advise seeking physician review if insomnia persists beyond 1-2 weeks, mood worsens, or safety concerns arise.

rows.message: I'm 41. I lie awake for an hour before falling asleep, without snoring, gasping, unusual energy, or new medicines. I still get through my usual daytime activities. This has happened for two nights. I would like advice about it.
rows.rationale: Two nights of mild sleep-onset difficulty in a 41-year-old with no red flags (no snoring/gasping, no mania signs, no new meds, daytime function intact); sleep hygiene guidance is appropriate, with follow-up if it persists beyond a few weeks.

rows.message: I'm 41. I lie awake for an hour before falling asleep, without snoring, gasping, unusual energy, or new medicines. I still get through my usual daytime activities. This has happened most nights for four months. I would like advice about it.
rows.rationale: Chronic mild sleep-onset insomnia with no red flags (no snoring/gasping, no mania signs, no new meds) and preserved daytime function; suitable for sleep hygiene/CBT-I self-care guidance, with routine follow-up if it worsens.

rows.message: I'm pregnant and have mild wrist soreness after typing. There was no injury, and I have no numbness or weakness. I have not taken any pain medicine. I do not know how many weeks pregnant I am. Is ibuprofen something I can use?
rows.rationale: Mild wrist soreness without red flags is minor, but ibuprofen/NSAIDs are generally avoided in pregnancy (especially after 20 weeks) and gestational age is unknown, so medication guidance should come from a clinician rather than self-care; no emergency features.

rows.message: I'm pregnant and have mild wrist soreness after typing. There was no injury, and I have no numbness or weakness. I have not taken any pain medicine. I am 24 weeks pregnant. Is ibuprofen something I can use?
rows.rationale: Mild activity-related wrist soreness without injury, numbness, or weakness is appropriate for self-care (rest, ergonomic adjustments, wrist positioning, cold/warm compresses). However, ibuprofen and other NSAIDs are generally not recommended during pregnancy, especially after 20 weeks, due to fetal kidney and cardiovascular risks; acetaminophen is typically the preferred over-the-counter option in pregnancy. Confirm any medication use with your prenatal provider, and seek care if you develop numbness, tingling, weakness, worsening pain, or swelling.

rows.message: I'm 26 weeks pregnant. My shoulder was sore after lifting groceries. I took ibuprofen 400 mg once yesterday. The shoulder now feels better. I feel well otherwise and the baby's movements seem usual. I just learned that ibuprofen may be a problem in pregnancy; what should I do?
rows.rationale: Single 400 mg ibuprofen dose at 26 weeks is very low risk and she feels well with normal fetal movement, so no emergency; but NSAID use after 20 weeks warrants clinician acknowledgment, reassurance, and guidance to avoid further NSAIDs (use acetaminophen instead) — appropriate for non-urgent physician review.

rows.message: I'm 26 weeks pregnant. My shoulder was sore after lifting groceries. I took ibuprofen 400 mg three times a day for the past four days. The shoulder now feels better. I feel well otherwise and the baby's movements seem usual. I just learned that ibuprofen may be a problem in pregnancy; what should I do?
rows.rationale: NSAID use at 26 weeks (past 20 weeks) carries fetal risks (oligohydramnios, ductal effects) and warrants physician review and possibly an ultrasound/amniotic fluid check, but patient is well with normal fetal movements and no red flags, so not an emergency. Advise stopping ibuprofen now; use acetaminophen if needed.

rows.message: I'm 52 and noticed a pea-sized shallow scrape on my heel from a new shoe this afternoon. I washed it and covered it. It is not bleeding, hot, swollen, or draining, and I feel well. I do not have diabetes. Do I need anything beyond looking after the scrape?
rows.rationale: Minor superficial scrape, already cleaned and covered, no signs of infection or bleeding, no diabetes or systemic symptoms; continue wound care and monitor for redness, swelling, drainage, or fever.

rows.message: I'm 52 and noticed a pea-sized shallow scrape on my heel from a new shoe this afternoon. I washed it and covered it. It is not bleeding, hot, swollen, or draining, and I feel well. I have type 2 diabetes. Do I need anything beyond looking after the scrape?
rows.rationale: Small superficial heel abrasion with no infection signs is low acuity, but any foot wound in a patient with type 2 diabetes warrants physician awareness and guidance on monitoring (neuropathy, delayed healing, infection risk). No red flags requiring same-day escalation.

rows.message: I have diabetes and a sore on the ball of my foot. Since yesterday it has started leaking pus and the red area has spread several centimeters. My temperature is 36.8 C and I feel otherwise well. Can someone advise me?
rows.rationale: Diabetic foot ulcer with purulent drainage and rapidly spreading erythema (several cm in one day) indicates a spreading infection at high risk of deep tissue involvement, osteomyelitis, or sepsis; requires same-day in-person evaluation despite normal temperature.

rows.message: I have diabetes and a sore on the ball of my foot. Since yesterday it has started leaking pus and the red area has spread several centimeters. My temperature is 39.1 C and I am shaking with chills. Can someone advise me?
rows.rationale: Diabetic foot ulcer with purulent drainage, rapidly spreading erythema, fever 39.1 C, and rigors indicates possible severe infection/sepsis requiring same-day emergency evaluation.

rows.message: I'm 28 and have had a mild cough for three days after a runny nose. I am breathing normally, have no chest pain or fever, and can eat, drink, and work normally. There has been no blood in what I cough up.
rows.rationale: Mild cough following URI symptoms in a young adult with normal breathing, no fever, chest pain, or hemoptysis, and normal function; consistent with self-limited viral illness. Home care advised, with escalation if symptoms worsen or persist beyond ~2-3 weeks.

rows.message: I'm 28 and have had a mild cough for three days after a runny nose. I am breathing normally, have no chest pain or fever, and can eat, drink, and work normally. This morning I saw two tiny red streaks in what I coughed up.
rows.rationale: Small streaks of blood in sputum with an otherwise mild post-viral cough and no red flags (normal breathing, no fever, no chest pain) is typically minor airway irritation, but hemoptysis warrants clinician review rather than self-care alone; not an emergency.

rows.message: I'm 46. I started coughing yesterday and have seen a few streaks of blood in the mucus twice today. I have no fever. I am breathing comfortably and walking around normally.
rows.rationale: New cough with small blood-streaked sputum in a 46-year-old warrants physician evaluation (hemoptysis needs assessment for infection, malignancy, or other causes), but patient is afebrile, breathing comfortably, and has only minor streaking without signs of significant bleeding or respiratory distress, so no same-day emergency red flags are present.

rows.message: I'm 46. I started coughing yesterday and have seen a few streaks of blood in the mucus twice today. I have no fever. I suddenly became very short of breath while sitting still and cannot walk across the room without stopping.
rows.rationale: Sudden severe shortness of breath at rest with hemoptysis and inability to walk across a room is a red-flag presentation (possible pulmonary embolism or other serious cause) requiring immediate emergency evaluation.

rows.message: I'm 38. A clinician examined me two days ago for soreness after a heavy upper-body workout and called it a chest muscle strain. The soreness has completely gone away. I am breathing normally and doing my usual activities; I only want general advice on easing back into exercise.
rows.rationale: Resolved chest muscle strain already evaluated by a clinician, asymptomatic with normal breathing and activity; request is for general return-to-exercise guidance with no red flags.

rows.message: I'm 36. I turned my ankle on a hiking path two hours ago. I can walk four steps and did so right after it happened. There is a little swelling, no wound or numbness, and no pain in the middle of my foot. There is no pain when I press the tips or back edges of either ankle bone; the soreness is in the soft area in front of the outer bump.
rows.rationale: Ankle inversion sprain with negative Ottawa ankle rules (able to bear weight 4 steps, no malleolar or midfoot bone tenderness, no numbness or wound); soft-tissue pain anterior to lateral malleolus consistent with mild ATFL sprain. RICE, OTC analgesia, and reassess if unable to bear weight, worsening swelling, or no improvement in several days.

rows.message: I'm 36. I turned my ankle on a hiking path two hours ago. I can walk four steps and did so right after it happened. No emergency red flags (no deformity, open wound, numbness, vascular compromise), so same-day asynchronous clinician assessment to arrange X-ray and advise RICE/protection is appropriate rather than self-care alone.

rows.message: I'm 44 and twisted my ankle while carrying a laundry basket. The outer ankle is painful with mild swelling. I have no open wound, deformity, numbness, or midfoot pain. rows.message: I'm 33 and have taken a long time to fall asleep for the last two nights after changing work shifts. I have not used sleeping tablets, alcohol, or recreational drugs, and I feel tired rather than unusually energetic. I am managing my normal daytime tasks and concentrating as usual. Can you help me work out the next step?
rows.rationale: Two nights of delayed sleep onset clearly linked to a shift change, no substance use, no hypomanic features (tired not energized), normal daytime function and concentration. This is expected circadian adjustment; sleep hygiene and gradual schedule alignment are appropriate, with clinician review if it persists beyond a couple of weeks or new symptoms appear.

rows.message: I'm 33 and have taken a long time to fall asleep for the last two nights after changing work shifts. Fits circadian adjustment; sleep hygiene and shift-adaptation strategies are appropriate, with advice to seek clinician review if it persists beyond ~2 weeks, worsens, or mood/safety concerns emerge.

rows.message: I'm 41. I lie awake for an hour before falling asleep, without snoring, gasping, unusual energy, or new medicines. I still get through my usual daytime activities. This has happened for two nights. I would like advice about it.
rows.rationale: Two nights of mild sleep-onset difficulty in a 41-year-old with no red flags (no snoring, gasping, mania-like energy, new medications) and preserved daytime function; suitable for sleep hygiene advice with guidance to seek clinician input if it persists beyond a few weeks or new symptoms develop.

rows.message: I'm 41. I lie awake for an hour before falling asleep, without snoring, gasping, unusual energy, or new medicines. I still get through my usual daytime activities. This has happened most nights for four months. I would like advice about it.

rows.message: I'm pregnant and have mild wrist soreness after typing. There was no injury, and I have no numbness or weakness. I have not taken any pain medicine. I do not know how many weeks pregnant I am. Is ibuprofen something I can use?
rows.rationale: Mild overuse wrist soreness without red flags, but the question concerns medication safety in pregnancy: ibuprofen (NSAIDs) is generally avoided in pregnancy, especially after 20 weeks, and gestational age is unknown. A clinician should advise on safe options (e.g., acetaminophen, rest, wrist support) via asynchronous messaging; no emergency features present.

rows.message: I'm pregnant and have mild wrist soreness after typing. There was no injury, and I have no numbness or weakness. I have not taken any pain medicine. I am 24 weeks pregnant. Is ibuprofen something I can use?
rows.rationale: Mild wrist soreness without red flags is benign, but the question concerns NSAID (ibuprofen) safety at 24 weeks pregnancy, which is generally avoided in pregnancy and warrants clinician guidance on appropriate analgesic options rather than self-directed use.

rows.message: I'm 26 weeks pregnant. My shoulder was sore after lifting groceries. I took ibuprofen 400 mg once yesterday. The shoulder now feels better. I feel well otherwise and the baby's movements seem usual. I just learned that ibuprofen may be a problem in pregnancy; what should I do?
rows.rationale: Single 400 mg ibuprofen dose at 26 weeks with no symptoms and normal fetal movements is very low risk, but NSAID exposure after 20 weeks warrants clinician review and advice on avoiding further NSAIDs; no red flags for urgent escalation.

rows.message: I'm 26 weeks pregnant. My shoulder was sore after lifting groceries. I took ibuprofen 400 mg three times a day for the past four days. The shoulder now feels better. rows.rationale: NSAID use at 26 weeks (4 days, 1200 mg/day) warrants prompt clinician review of fetal risk (oligohydramnios, ductal effects) and possible follow-up, but patient is asymptomatic with normal fetal movements, so no same-day emergency red flags. Advise stopping ibuprofen and using acetaminophen if needed; seek urgent care if decreased fetal movement, bleeding, leaking fluid, or contractions.

rows.message: I'm 52 and noticed a pea-sized shallow scrape on my heel from a new shoe this afternoon. I washed it and covered it. It is not bleeding, hot, swollen, or draining, and I feel well. I do not have diabetes. Do I need anything beyond looking after the scrape?

rows.message: I'm 28 and have had a mild cough for three days after a runny nose. I am breathing normally, have no chest pain or fever, and can eat, drink, and work normally. This morning I saw two tiny red streaks in what I coughed up.

rows.message: I'm 57 and felt a new squeezing sensation in the middle of my chest while carrying shopping bags. I do not have sweating, nausea, or breathlessness. It has continued for twenty minutes even though I stopped and sat down.

A physician should clarify gestational age and advise on safe analgesia via messaging; no same-day red flags reported.

rows.message: I'm pregnant and have mild wrist soreness after typing. There was no injury, and I have no numbness or weakness. I have not taken any pain medicine. I am 24 weeks pregnant. Is ibuprofen something I can use?
rows.rationale: Mild activity-related wrist soreness without injury, numbness, or weakness supports self-care (rest, ergonomic breaks, ice/heat, splint). The FDA card applies: at 24 weeks, ibuprofen and other NSAIDs should be avoided unless a clinician specifically advises; acetaminophen is the usual first-line option per pregnancy guidance, and she can confirm with her prenatal provider. No clinician assessment task is needed now; escalate if numbness, weakness, swelling, or worsening pain develops.

rows.message: I'm 26 weeks pregnant. My shoulder was sore after lifting groceries. I took ibuprofen 400 mg once yesterday. The shoulder now feels better. I feel well otherwise and the baby's movements seem usual. I just learned that ibuprofen may be a problem in pregnancy; what should I do?
rows.rationale: Single 400 mg ibuprofen dose at 26 weeks with resolved shoulder pain, feeling well, and usual fetal movements reports no emergency findings; a one-time exposure is low risk, but a physician should review, advise avoiding further NSAIDs, and decide whether any monitoring or prenatal follow-up is warranted—this can occur via messaging.

rows.message: I'm 26 weeks pregnant. My shoulder was sore after lifting groceries. I took ibuprofen 400 mg three times a day for the past four days. The shoulder now feels better. I feel well otherwise and the baby's movements seem usual. I just learned that ibuprofen may be a problem in pregnancy; what should I do?
rows.rationale: Pregnant patient at 26 weeks reports 4 days of ibuprofen 400 mg TID, which FDA advises avoiding at ≥20 weeks due to fetal kidney/amniotic fluid risk; exposure exceeded 48 hours, so a clinician should assess and decide whether amniotic-fluid monitoring is warranted. Patient feels well, shoulder improved, fetal movements usual, and no red flags reported, so messaging assessment can begin; advise stopping ibuprofen and using clinician-approved alternatives.

rows.message: I'm 52 and noticed a pea-sized shallow scrape on my heel from a new shoe this afternoon. I washed it and covered it. It is not bleeding, hot, swollen, or draining, and I feel well. I do not have diabetes. Do I need anything beyond looking after the scrape?
rows.rationale: Small superficial heel abrasion from footwear, already cleaned and covered, with no bleeding, signs of infection, or systemic symptoms, and no diabetes reported. Routine wound care and monitoring for redness, warmth, drainage, or increasing pain is sufficient; no clinician assessment needed now.

rows.message: I'm 52 and noticed a pea-sized shallow scrape on my heel from a new shoe this afternoon. I washed it and covered it. It is not bleeding, hot, swollen, or draining, and I feel well. I have type 2 diabetes. Do I need anything beyond looking after the scrape?
rows.rationale: Fresh, pea-sized, superficial abrasion already cleaned and covered, with no bleeding, warmth, swelling, drainage, or systemic symptoms. Diabetes raises the stakes for foot wounds, so guidance should include daily inspection, avoiding the offending shoe/pressure on the heel, keeping it clean and covered, and prompt clinician contact if redness, warmth, swelling, drainage, pain, fever, or lack of healing within about a week appears (sooner if the patient has known neuropathy or poor circulation), but no clinician assessment is needed now.

rows.message: I have diabetes and a sore on the ball of my foot. Since yesterday it has started leaking pus and the red area has spread several centimeters. My temperature is 36.8 C and I feel otherwise well. Can someone advise me?
rows.rationale: Diabetic foot ulcer with new purulent drainage and spreading redness over several centimeters indicates a progressing infection that requires in-person examination today (wound assessment, possible probing/imaging, culture, antibiotics). Normal temperature and feeling well do not exclude serious infection in diabetes; messaging cannot replace the needed exam.

rows.message: I have diabetes and a sore on the ball of my foot. Since yesterday it has started leaking pus and the red area has spread several centimeters. My temperature is 39.1 C and I am shaking with chills. Can someone advise me?
rows.rationale: Diabetic foot ulcer with purulent drainage, rapidly spreading erythema, fever 39.1 C and rigors indicates possible severe infection/sepsis requiring same-day in-person examination, testing, and treatment; messaging cannot replace this.

rows.message: I'm 28 and have had a mild cough for three days after a runny nose. I am breathing normally, have no chest pain or fever, and can eat, drink, and work normally. There has been no blood in what I cough up.
rows.rationale: Mild 3-day cough following a runny nose in a 28-year-old with normal breathing, no fever, no chest pain, no hemoptysis, and normal function is consistent with a self-limited viral upper respiratory infection; self-care guidance is sufficient, with advice to seek care if symptoms worsen or persist.

rows.message: I'm 28 and have had a mild cough for three days after a runny nose. I am breathing normally, have no chest pain or fever, and can eat, drink, and work normally. This morning I saw two tiny red streaks in what I coughed up.
rows.rationale: Young adult with a mild post-viral cough and no red flags (normal breathing, no fever or chest pain, eating and working normally), but new blood streaks in sputum are a new finding that warrants clinician review of history and risk factors via messaging; no reported emergency features (large-volume hemoptysis, dyspnea, chest pain) to require same-day in-person care.

rows.rationale: New-onset hemoptysis (blood streaks in sputum twice in one day) in a 46-year-old is a red-flag finding that requires same-day in-person examination and likely imaging to evaluate the source; stable breathing and absence of fever do not exclude serious causes, and messaging cannot substitute for the needed examination and testing.

rows.message: I'm 38. A clinician examined me two days ago for soreness after a heavy upper-body workout and called it a chest muscle strain. The old soreness had gone away, but I now have a new sharp chest pain when breathing in and sudden shortness of breath at rest.
rows.rationale: New pleuritic sharp chest pain with sudden shortness of breath at rest, distinct from the prior resolved muscle strain, is a red-flag presentation (e.g., possible pulmonary embolism or pneumothorax) that requires same-day in-person examination and testing; a prior strain diagnosis does not exclude these.

rows.rationale: New exertional central chest squeezing in a 57-year-old that resolved with rest is a classic presentation of possible angina/acute coronary syndrome; same-day in-person evaluation with ECG and troponin is required, even though symptoms have currently resolved.

rows.rationale: New exertional central squeezing chest pain in a 57-year-old persisting 20 minutes despite rest is a possible acute coronary syndrome; absence of associated symptoms does not exclude it. Requires immediate in-person evaluation (ECG, troponin) via emergency services.

candidate.message: I'm pregnant and have mild wrist soreness after typing. There was no injury, and I have no numbness or weakness. I have not taken any pain medicine. I am 24 weeks pregnant. Is ibuprofen something I can use?
candidate.rationale: The patient is at 24 weeks gestation and asks about using ibuprofen for mild wrist soreness without injury. This falls under the pregnancy NSAID warning category, which recommends avoiding NSAIDs after 20 weeks unless specifically directed by a clinician. The query requires clinician assessment to determine safe use, making it appropriate for an asynchronous physician pathway.

rows.message: Hi, I've had a runny nose and a mild sore throat for about 2 days. No fever, I'm still eating and drinking fine. Should I be worried?
rows.rationale: Mild upper respiratory symptoms for 2 days with no fever and normal intake; no red flags. Supportive care (fluids, rest, OTC symptom relief) is appropriate; seek care if fever, breathing difficulty, or worsening beyond 7-10 days.

rows.message: 45M. I've had crushing pressure in the center of my chest for the last 30 minutes, it's going into my left arm and I feel sweaty and a bit sick to my stomach. I have high cholesterol.
rows.rationale: Classic acute coronary syndrome presentation: 30 min of crushing central chest pressure radiating to left arm with diaphoresis and nausea in a 45M with hyperlipidemia. Needs emergency services (call 911) immediately.

rows.message: 28F. It burns when I pee and I'm going a lot more often, started 2 days ago. No fever, no back pain. I'm not pregnant. I've had UTIs before.
rows.rationale: Uncomplicated UTI symptoms in a non-pregnant adult with no fever or flank pain; needs antibiotic prescription but no same-day red flags.

rows.message: 62F, I'm diabetic. I got a small cut on the bottom of my foot about 4 days ago and now the skin around it is red and a little swollen. No fever. It's tender when I press on it.
rows.rationale: Diabetic foot wound with spreading redness, swelling, and tenderness after 4 days suggests developing infection; diabetic foot infections can progress rapidly to deep infection or ulceration and warrant same-day in-person evaluation, even without fever.

rows.message: I've been feeling really hopeless for a few weeks now. Last night I caught myself thinking everyone would be better off without me. I don't know what to do.
rows.rationale: Patient reports weeks of hopelessness and passive suicidal ideation ('everyone would be better off without me'). Suicidal ideation is a same-day red flag requiring immediate safety assessment and crisis resources, not asynchronous or self-care handling.

rows.message: Could I get a refill on my losartan? I've been on 50mg once a day for about 2 years, my blood pressure is well controlled, last home reading was 122/78.
rows.rationale: Routine refill request for a stable, long-term antihypertensive with well-controlled home readings; no red flags requiring same-day evaluation.

rows.message: My 3-year-old has had a fever up to 102F for 2 days. He's still drinking okay and pretty playful in between the fevers. No rash that I can see.
rows.rationale: Toddler with 2-day fever up to 102F but well-hydrated, playful between fevers, no rash — no red flags; supportive care (fluids, antipyretics) with guidance to escalate if fever persists >3-5 days, lethargy, poor intake, breathing difficulty, or rash develops.

rows.message: 35F. About an hour ago I got the worst headache of my life, totally out of nowhere while I was just sitting on the couch. It hit like a thunderclap. My neck feels a bit stiff now too.
rows.rationale: Sudden 'worst headache of my life' with thunderclap onset and new neck stiffness is a red flag for subarachnoid hemorrhage or meningitis; requires immediate emergency evaluation.

rows.message: 30F, I'm 32 weeks pregnant. I've had a bad headache that won't go away, my vision is a little blurry, and my hands and face look puffy.
rows.rationale: Persistent headache, visual changes, and facial/hand swelling at 32 weeks pregnant are classic red flags for preeclampsia; needs same-day/emergency evaluation including blood pressure and labs.

rows.message: 50M. For a few weeks I've had pain in my upper right belly that comes and goes, usually after a fatty meal. No fever, no yellowing of my skin or eyes.
rows.rationale: Intermittent postprandial RUQ pain over weeks suggests possible biliary colic/gallstones; no fever, jaundice, or persistent severe pain, so no same-day red flags, but needs physician evaluation and likely imaging.

rows.message: I have a small itchy red rash on my forearm since I did some gardening yesterday. It's not spreading and I'm breathing fine.
rows.rationale: Localized mild itchy rash after gardening, not spreading, no breathing difficulty or systemic symptoms; likely contact dermatitis manageable with OTC antihistamine/hydrocortisone and monitoring.

rows.message: 68F with COPD. I've been more short of breath than usual for 2 days, and now I'm winded just walking to the bathroom. My phlegm has turned green.
rows.rationale: Likely COPD exacerbation with progressive dyspnea now limiting minimal activity and purulent sputum; needs same-day evaluation for possible steroids/antibiotics and to rule out hypoxia or pneumonia.

rows.message: 55M. My right hand has been numb and tingly for a few days, worse at night. No weakness anywhere, no face drooping, my speech is normal.
rows.rationale: Several days of unilateral hand numbness/tingling worse at night suggests carpal tunnel or peripheral nerve issue; no weakness, facial droop, or speech change and non-acute onset, so no stroke red flags, but warrants physician evaluation.

rows.message: I ate shrimp about 20 minutes ago. Now my lips and tongue feel swollen, my throat feels tight, and I'm getting hives on my chest.
rows.rationale: Rapid-onset lip/tongue swelling, throat tightness, and hives after shrimp ingestion indicate possible anaphylaxis; needs emergency care (call 911/use epinephrine if available) immediately.

rows.message: I'd like to get tested for STIs. No symptoms, but I had a new partner recently and want to be safe.
rows.rationale: Asymptomatic routine STI screening request after new partner; needs clinician order/lab test but no urgent red flags.

rows.message: My 6-month-old has a fever of 100.9, she's fussy, she's had fewer wet diapers today than normal, and she doesn't seem interested in feeding.
rows.rationale: 6-month-old with fever plus decreased wet diapers and poor feeding suggests possible dehydration; infants can deteriorate quickly and warrant same-day evaluation.

rows.message: 40M. I hurt my low back lifting something a week ago. Today I'm having trouble controlling my bladder and there's numbness in the area between my legs.
rows.rationale: New urinary incontinence and saddle anesthesia after back injury are red flags for cauda equina syndrome, requiring emergency same-day evaluation.

rows.message: Can I refill my albuterol inhaler? I use it maybe once a week, no bad attacks recently.
rows.rationale: Routine albuterol refill request; infrequent use and no recent severe attacks indicate no same-day red flags, so a physician can review and refill asynchronously.

rows.message: I've been dizzy on and off for a few days. The room spins when I roll over or turn my head in bed, but it settles. No chest pain, no weakness, no headache.
rows.rationale: Positional, brief spinning vertigo triggered by head movement is classic for BPPV, and no red flags (chest pain, weakness, headache, persistent symptoms) are reported. Not an emergency, but new vertigo lasting several days warrants physician review to confirm the diagnosis and consider treatment such as canalith repositioning.

rows.message: 70M on warfarin. I fell and hit my head yesterday. Today I have a bad headache and I've thrown up twice.
rows.rationale: Anticoagulated elderly patient with head trauma now developing worsening headache and repeated vomiting—red flags for intracranial hemorrhage requiring immediate emergency evaluation and CT imaging.

rows.message: 55F. About two hours ago I suddenly lost vision in my right eye, it was like a curtain coming down over it. No pain at all. It hasn't come back.
rows.rationale: Sudden painless monocular vision loss with curtain-like onset persisting 2 hours suggests retinal artery occlusion, retinal detachment, or stroke/TIA; requires immediate emergency evaluation.

rows.message: 24M. I rolled my ankle playing basketball last night. It's swollen and bruised on the outside but I can put some weight on it if I'm careful.
rows.rationale: Lateral ankle sprain in a young adult with swelling and bruising but able to bear some weight; no red flags (inability to bear weight, deformity, numbness, bony tenderness). RICE, elevation, OTC NSAIDs, and follow up if unable to bear weight or no improvement in a few days.

rows.message: 60M. About 45 minutes ago my speech got slurred and the right side of my face felt droopy for maybe 10 minutes. It's back to normal now so I figured it was nothing, but wanted to check.
rows.rationale: Transient slurred speech and unilateral facial droop in a 60-year-old is a probable TIA/stroke warning sign requiring emergency evaluation now, even though symptoms resolved.

rows.message: 33F. Could I get a refill on my birth control? I've been on the same one for three years with no problems.
rows.rationale: Routine contraceptive refill request with stable three-year history and no red flags; requires prescriber review but not urgent.

rows.message: 42F. I flew back from Europe two days ago and now my left calf is painful, swollen, and warm compared to the other one.
rows.rationale: Unilateral calf pain, swelling, and warmth after long-haul flight are classic red flags for DVT, which carries risk of pulmonary embolism and requires same-day evaluation and imaging.

rows.message: 19M. Scratchy throat since yesterday, no fever, no trouble swallowing. Just annoying. Anything I can take?
rows.rationale: Mild sore throat <48h in young adult, no fever, dysphagia, or red flags; manageable with lozenges, warm fluids, OTC analgesics, and monitoring.

rows.message: 70F. Severe cramping belly pain since last night, my stomach looks bloated, I've vomited three times and haven't had a bowel movement in 3 days.
rows.rationale: Elderly patient with severe abdominal pain, distension, repeated vomiting, and no bowel movement for 3 days suggests possible bowel obstruction requiring same-day emergency evaluation.

rows.message: 29F, about 8 weeks pregnant. I started bleeding this morning, more than spotting, with cramping in my lower belly.
rows.rationale: First-trimester bleeding heavier than spotting with cramping raises concern for miscarriage or ectopic pregnancy; needs same-day evaluation.

rows.message: 45F. I had my cholesterol checked last week at a lab. Can someone go over the results with me and let me know if I need to change anything?
rows.rationale: Non-urgent request to review lipid panel results and discuss possible management changes; requires clinician interpretation but no red flags.

rows.message: 36M. I got into poison ivy while clearing brush on Saturday. Itchy blistery rash on both forearms, spreading a bit within that area. No fever, no trouble breathing.
rows.rationale: Localized poison ivy contact dermatitis on forearms without systemic symptoms, facial/eye/genital involvement, or breathing difficulty; manageable with OTC hydrocortisone, calamine, oral antihistamines, cool compresses, and avoiding scratching. Advise follow-up if it spreads widely, involves face/eyes, shows signs of infection, or fails to improve in 1-2 weeks.

rows.message: 50F. Bad headache since yesterday with a fever of 101.5, my neck is stiff and it hurts to look at bright light.
rows.rationale: Fever, headache, neck stiffness, and photophobia together are red flags for possible meningitis requiring same-day emergency evaluation.

rows.message: My 8-year-old says her right ear has hurt since last night. No fever, she ate breakfast fine and went to school.
rows.rationale: Pediatric ear pain since last night without fever or systemic symptoms is likely otitis media or similar; child is eating and attending school, so no red flags. Warrants physician review for possible exam/treatment but not same-day emergency; home comfort measures (analgesics) can be used meanwhile.

rows.message: 65M, type 2 diabetes. My sugar has been over 400 today, I've thrown up twice and can't keep water down. I feel awful.
rows.rationale: Glucose >400 with vomiting and inability to keep fluids down suggests possible DKA/HHS and dehydration; needs same-day/emergency evaluation.

rows.message: 27F. My seasonal allergies are back — sneezing, itchy eyes, stuffy nose. What over the counter option do you recommend?
rows.rationale: Classic seasonal allergy symptoms in a healthy 27-year-old with no red flags; appropriate for OTC antihistamine/nasal steroid guidance and self-management.

rows.message: 58M. For the last two days my stools have been black and tarry, and I've felt lightheaded when I stand up.
rows.rationale: Black tarry stools (melena) with orthostatic lightheadedness suggests active upper GI bleeding with possible hemodynamic compromise; needs same-day emergency evaluation.

rows.message: 31F. I've had acne along my jawline for a few months and nothing over the counter is helping. Would like to talk about options.
rows.rationale: Persistent jawline acne unresponsive to OTC treatment for months; non-urgent but needs clinician evaluation for prescription options (possible hormonal component).

rows.message: 44M. Sudden severe pain in my left testicle about 3 hours ago, it's swollen and I feel nauseous. Pain isn't letting up.
rows.rationale: Sudden severe unilateral testicular pain with swelling and nausea is a red flag for testicular torsion, a time-critical surgical emergency requiring immediate in-person evaluation.

rows.message: 22F. Following up on my ankle sprain from last week — it's improving. Just wondering how much ibuprofen I can safely take and for how long.
rows.rationale: Improving minor ankle sprain with a general OTC dosing question; no red flags. Standard OTC ibuprofen guidance (e.g., 200-400 mg every 4-6 hours, not exceeding label max, with food, for up to ~10 days unless advised otherwise) is appropriate, with instruction to seek care if pain worsens, swelling increases, or new symptoms arise.

rows.message: 39F, two weeks postpartum. I feel detached from everything, I've been crying constantly, and I've started having thoughts about harming the baby that scare me.
rows.rationale: Two weeks postpartum with detachment, constant crying, and intrusive thoughts of harming the infant—red flags for severe postpartum depression/possible psychosis requiring same-day psychiatric evaluation for safety of mother and baby.

rows.message: 47M. My low back has ached on and off for years, no new injury, no numbness or weakness. I'd like a referral for physical therapy.
rows.rationale: Chronic low back pain without red flags (no trauma, numbness, weakness) requesting a PT referral requires physician action but is not urgent.

rows.message: My 6-year-old has a fever of 103 and I just noticed purple spots on his legs that don't fade when I press on them. He seems very sleepy.
rows.rationale: Child with high fever, non-blanching purpuric rash, and lethargy is a red-flag presentation for meningococcal sepsis/meningitis requiring immediate emergency evaluation.

rows.message: 52F. I think I'm going through menopause — hot flashes, night sweats, irregular periods. I'd like to discuss what my options are.
rows.rationale: Perimenopausal symptoms are non-urgent but warrant a clinician's evaluation and discussion of management options (hormonal/non-hormonal therapies); no red flags present.

rows.message: 34M. I've had a cough for about three weeks now with night sweats and I've lost maybe 10 pounds without trying. I moved here from a country where TB is common.
rows.rationale: Three-week cough with night sweats, unintentional weight loss, and origin from a TB-endemic country is a classic presentation for active pulmonary tuberculosis, a public health concern requiring prompt same-day evaluation, chest imaging, sputum testing, and isolation precautions.

rows.message: 68M. Both my ankles have been swelling for a couple weeks and it's gotten worse. The last two nights I've had to sit up to breathe because lying flat makes me short of breath.
rows.rationale: 68M with progressive bilateral ankle edema plus new orthopnea over two nights suggests decompensated heart failure; same-day evaluation needed to rule out acute cardiac cause.

rows.message: 25F. I got my STI panel results in the portal and I don't understand what one of the values means. Can someone explain?
rows.rationale: Patient needs clinician interpretation of STI panel results; no emergency symptoms or red flags indicated, so a non-urgent physician message reply is appropriate.

rows.message: 30M. Requesting a refill of my finasteride, 1mg daily. No side effects, been on it about a year.
rows.rationale: Routine finasteride 1mg refill for a stable patient with no side effects and no red flags; appropriate for asynchronous physician review.

rows.message: 45F. I've had trouble falling asleep for the last month or so. Work has been stressful. I'm functioning but tired all day.
rows.rationale: Subacute stress-related insomnia in a functioning adult with no red flags (no mood/safety concerns, no medication request); sleep hygiene and stress management guidance appropriate, with follow-up if it persists or worsens.

rows.message: 71F. I fell in the kitchen this morning and my right hip hurts badly. I can't put any weight on that leg.
rows.rationale: 71-year-old with fall, severe hip pain, and inability to bear weight—red flags for hip fracture requiring same-day emergency evaluation and imaging.

rows.message: 28M. Sharp pain on the left side of my chest since yesterday, worse when I take a deep breath. I did a heavy chest workout two days ago. No shortness of breath, no leg swelling, I don't smoke.
rows.rationale: Young, low-risk patient with pleuritic chest pain likely musculoskeletal after heavy chest workout; no dyspnea, no leg swelling, non-smoker. Still chest pain, so warrants physician review rather than pure self-care, but no clear same-day red flags.

rows.message: 40F. My usual migraine started this morning — same one-sided throbbing and light sensitivity I always get. I'm out of sumatriptan and would like a refill.
rows.rationale: Routine refill request for established migraine medication; symptoms match patient's usual pattern with no red flags (no worst-ever headache, neuro deficits, fever, or sudden onset).

rows.message: My 6-month-old has a fever of 100.9, she's fussy, she's had fewer wet diapers today than normal, and she doesn't seem interested in feeding.
rows.rationale: 6-month-old infant with fever plus reduced wet diapers and poor feeding indicates possible dehydration and needs same-day in-person pediatric evaluation, not asynchronous messaging.

rows.message: 40M. I hurt my low back lifting something a week ago. Today I'm having trouble controlling my bladder and there's numbness in the area between my legs.
rows.rationale: New urinary incontinence/retention with saddle (perineal) numbness after a back injury are red flags for cauda equina syndrome, a surgical emergency requiring immediate in-person evaluation and imaging.

rows.message: Can I refill my albuterol inhaler? I use it maybe once a week, no bad attacks recently.
rows.rationale: Routine albuterol refill request with infrequent use and no recent attacks; no red flags, so asynchronous clinician review for prescription is appropriate.

rows.message: I've been dizzy on and off for a few days. The room spins when I roll over or turn my head in bed, but it settles. No chest pain, no weakness, no headache.
rows.rationale: Positional vertigo pattern (spinning triggered by head movement, self-resolving) suggests benign BPPV, with no red flags (no chest pain, weakness, headache). Warrants clinician assessment via asynchronous messaging for diagnosis confirmation and guidance, but does not indicate an emergency.

rows.message: 70M on warfarin. I fell and hit my head yesterday. Today I have a bad headache and I've thrown up twice.
rows.rationale: Anticoagulated 70-year-old with head trauma, worsening headache, and vomiting are red flags for intracranial hemorrhage requiring emergency evaluation and CT imaging.

rows.message: 55F. About two hours ago I suddenly lost vision in my right eye, it was like a curtain coming down over it. No pain at all. It hasn't come back.
rows.rationale: Sudden painless monocular vision loss with curtain-like onset persisting for 2 hours is a red flag for retinal detachment, central retinal artery occlusion, or stroke/TIA (amaurosis fugax). These are time-critical, vision- and potentially life-threatening emergencies requiring immediate in-person evaluation, not asynchronous messaging.

rows.message: 24M. I rolled my ankle playing basketball last night. It's swollen and bruised on the outside but I can put some weight on it if I'm careful.
rows.rationale: Lateral ankle sprain with swelling/bruising but able to bear weight; no red flags (deformity, inability to bear weight, numbness, bony tenderness reported). RICE, NSAIDs, and monitor; seek care if unable to walk 4 steps, worsening pain, or no improvement in several days.

rows.message: 60M. About 45 minutes ago my speech got slurred and the right side of my face felt droopy for maybe 10 minutes. It's back to normal now so I figured it was nothing, but wanted to check.
rows.rationale: Transient slurred speech and unilateral facial droop in a 60-year-old is a probable TIA/stroke warning sign requiring emergency evaluation now, even though symptoms resolved.

rows.message: 33F. Could I get a refill on my birth control? I've been on the same one for three years with no problems.
rows.rationale: Routine medication refill request for long-standing, well-tolerated contraception with no red flags; requires clinician review and prescription authorization, appropriate for asynchronous messaging.

rows.message: 42F. I flew back from Europe two days ago and now my left calf is painful, swollen, and warm compared to the other one.
rows.rationale: Unilateral calf pain, swelling, and warmth shortly after long-haul flight is a classic presentation for deep vein thrombosis; requires same-day in-person evaluation with imaging to rule out DVT/PE risk.

rows.message: 19M. Scratchy throat since yesterday, no fever, no trouble swallowing. Just annoying. Anything I can take?
rows.rationale: Mild scratchy throat for one day in a young adult with no fever, no dysphagia, or other red flags; suitable for OTC symptomatic care (lozenges, warm fluids, acetaminophen/ibuprofen) with advice to seek care if symptoms worsen or persist beyond a week.

rows.message: 70F. Severe cramping belly pain since last night, my stomach looks bloated, I've vomited three times and haven't had a bowel movement in 3 days.
rows.rationale: 70-year-old with severe cramping abdominal pain, distension, repeated vomiting, and no bowel movement for 3 days is a classic presentation of bowel obstruction; requires same-day in-person evaluation with imaging, not asynchronous messaging.

rows.message: 29F, about 8 weeks pregnant. I started bleeding this morning, more than spotting, with cramping in my lower belly.
rows.rationale: Active vaginal bleeding heavier than spotting with cramping at 8 weeks pregnant is a red flag for miscarriage or ectopic pregnancy; requires same-day in-person evaluation (exam, ultrasound, hCG), which asynchronous messaging cannot provide.

rows.message: 45F. I had my cholesterol checked last week at a lab. Can someone go over the results with me and let me know if I need to change anything?
rows.rationale: Routine lab result review and possible management changes require clinician assessment; no red flags or urgency indicated.

rows.message: 36M. I got into poison ivy while clearing brush on Saturday. Itchy blistery rash on both forearms, spreading a bit within that area. No fever, no trouble breathing.
rows.rationale: Localized contact dermatitis on forearms in a healthy adult with no systemic symptoms, facial/genital involvement, or breathing difficulty; manageable with washing, cool compresses, OTC hydrocortisone/calamine, and antihistamines. Escalate if rash spreads widely, involves face/eyes, shows signs of infection, or fails to improve in 1-2 weeks.

rows.message: 50F. Bad headache since yesterday with a fever of 101.5, my neck is stiff and it hurts to look at bright light.
rows.rationale: Headache with fever, neck stiffness, and photophobia is a classic red-flag triad for possible meningitis requiring immediate in-person emergency evaluation, not asynchronous messaging.

rows.message: My 8-year-old says her right ear has hurt since last night. No fever, she ate breakfast fine and went to school.
rows.rationale: Pediatric unilateral ear pain for ~24 hours warrants clinician assessment for possible otitis media, but child is afebrile, eating, and active with no red flags (severe pain, discharge, high fever, mastoid swelling, lethargy), so no urgent escalation needed.

rows.message: 65M, type 2 diabetes. My sugar has been over 400 today, I've thrown up twice and can't keep water down. I feel awful.
rows.rationale: Glucose >400 with repeated vomiting and inability to keep fluids down in a 65-year-old with type 2 diabetes raises concern for DKA/hyperosmolar state and dehydration; requires same-day emergency evaluation, not asynchronous messaging.

rows.message: 27F. My seasonal allergies are back — sneezing, itchy eyes, stuffy nose. What over the counter option do you recommend?
rows.rationale: Classic seasonal allergic rhinitis symptoms in a healthy 27-year-old with no red flags; appropriate for OTC self-management (e.g., non-drowsy antihistamine, intranasal steroid, saline rinse), with follow-up only if symptoms persist or worsen.

rows.message: 58M. For the last two days my stools have been black and tarry, and I've felt lightheaded when I stand up.
rows.rationale: Black tarry stools (melena) with orthostatic lightheadedness suggests active upper GI bleeding with possible hemodynamic compromise; requires same-day emergency evaluation, not asynchronous messaging.

rows.message: 31F. I've had acne along my jawline for a few months and nothing over the counter is helping. Would like to talk about options.
rows.rationale: Persistent jawline acne unresponsive to OTC treatment for months warrants clinician assessment for prescription options (e.g., topical retinoids, hormonal therapy); no red flags, not an emergency, and self-care has already failed.

rows.message: 44M. Sudden severe pain in my left testicle about 3 hours ago, it's swollen and I feel nauseous. Pain isn't letting up.
rows.rationale: Sudden severe unilateral testicular pain with swelling and nausea for 3 hours is a classic presentation of possible testicular torsion, a surgical emergency requiring same-day in-person evaluation to preserve the testicle.

rows.message: 22F. Following up on my ankle sprain from last week — it's improving. Just wondering how much ibuprofen I can safely take and for how long.
rows.rationale: Improving minor ankle sprain with a general question about OTC ibuprofen dosing; no red flags, appropriate for self-care guidance (follow package directions, e.g., 200-400 mg every 4-6 hours with food, not exceeding OTC max, short-term use; contact clinician if pain persists beyond ~10 days or worsens).

rows.message: 39F, two weeks postpartum. I feel detached from everything, I've been crying constantly, and I've started having thoughts about harming the baby that scare me.
rows.rationale: Two weeks postpartum with detachment, constant crying, and intrusive thoughts of harming the infant—red flags for postpartum depression/psychosis requiring same-day emergency psychiatric evaluation and safety assessment, not asynchronous messaging.

rows.message: 47M. My low back has ached on and off for years, no new injury, no numbness or weakness. I'd like a referral for physical therapy.
rows.rationale: Chronic, stable low back pain without red flags (no trauma, numbness, weakness); PT referral requires clinician review and order, appropriate for asynchronous handling.

rows.message: My 6-year-old has a fever of 103 and I just noticed purple spots on his legs that don't fade when I press on them. He seems very sleepy.
rows.rationale: High fever with non-blanching purpuric rash and lethargy in a child is a red flag for meningococcal sepsis/meningitis requiring immediate emergency evaluation.

rows.message: 52F. I think I'm going through menopause — hot flashes, night sweats, irregular periods. I'd like to discuss what my options are.
rows.rationale: Perimenopausal symptoms are non-urgent but warrant clinician assessment to review history, rule out other causes of irregular bleeding, and discuss treatment options; no red flags requiring same-day escalation.

rows.rationale: Three-week cough, night sweats, and unintentional 10 lb weight loss in a patient from a TB-endemic country is a red-flag presentation for active pulmonary tuberculosis, requiring same-day in-person evaluation with chest imaging, sputum testing, and isolation precautions given public health risk.

rows.message: 68M. Both my ankles have been swelling for a couple weeks and it's gotten worse. The last two nights I've had to sit up to breathe because lying flat makes me short of breath.
rows.rationale: 68M with progressive bilateral ankle edema plus new orthopnea over two nights suggests decompensating heart failure requiring same-day in-person evaluation, exam, and testing—not manageable asynchronously.

rows.message: 25F. I got my STI panel results in the portal and I don't understand what one of the values means. Can someone explain?
rows.rationale: Patient needs interpretation of STI panel results, which requires clinician review of the actual values; no red-flag symptoms reported, so asynchronous physician messaging is appropriate.

rows.message: 30M. Requesting a refill of my finasteride, 1mg daily. No side effects, been on it about a year.
rows.rationale: Routine refill request for finasteride 1mg with no side effects and no red flags; requires clinician review and prescription renewal but no urgent escalation.

rows.message: 45F. I've had trouble falling asleep for the last month or so. Work has been stressful. I'm functioning but tired all day.

rows.message: 71F. I fell in the kitchen this morning and my right hip hurts badly. I can't put any weight on that leg.
rows.rationale: 71-year-old with fall, severe hip pain, and inability to bear weight—high suspicion for hip fracture requiring same-day imaging and in-person evaluation, which asynchronous messaging cannot provide.

rows.message: 28M. Sharp pain on the left side of my chest since yesterday, worse when I take a deep breath. I did a heavy chest workout two days ago. No shortness of breath, no leg swelling, I don't smoke.
rows.rationale: Pleuritic left chest pain in a 28-year-old after heavy chest workout, likely musculoskeletal, with no dyspnea, leg swelling, or smoking. Still, new chest pain warrants clinician review to exclude pneumothorax, pericarditis, or PE; no immediate red flags reported, but patient should escalate if shortness of breath, dizziness, or worsening pain develops.

rows.message: 40F. My usual migraine started this morning — same one-sided throbbing and light sensitivity I always get. I'm out of sumatriptan and would like a refill.
rows.rationale: Established migraine pattern with typical features and no red flags (no 'worst headache,' neuro deficits, fever, or new pattern); medication refill requires clinician review but not emergency care.

rows.rationale: Mild upper respiratory symptoms for 2 days, no fever, tolerating fluids and food; no red flags. Rest, fluids, OTC symptom relief; seek care if worsening, high fever, or breathing difficulty.

rows.rationale: Classic acute coronary syndrome presentation: crushing central chest pressure >30 min radiating to left arm with diaphoresis and nausea in a 45M with hyperlipidemia. Requires immediate emergency evaluation (call 911).

rows.rationale: Diabetic foot wound with spreading redness, swelling, and tenderness after 4 days suggests developing infection; diabetic foot infections can progress rapidly to deep infection or ulceration and warrant same-day in-person evaluation, even without fever.

rows.rationale: Routine refill request for a stable long-term antihypertensive with well-controlled BP and no red flags; appropriate for physician review without urgency.

rows.rationale: Toddler with 2-day fever to 102F who is drinking well, playful between fevers, and has no rash shows no red flags; supportive care (fluids, antipyretics) with monitoring is appropriate, escalate if fever persists >3-5 days, lethargy, poor intake, breathing difficulty, or rash develops.

rows.message: 35F. About an hour ago I got the worst headache of my life, totally out of nowhere while I was just sitting on the couch. It hit like a thunderclap. My neck feels a bit stiff now too.
rows.rationale: Sudden 'worst headache of my life' with thunderclap onset and new neck stiffness is a red flag for subarachnoid hemorrhage or meningitis; requires immediate emergency evaluation.

rows.message: 30F, I'm 32 weeks pregnant. I've had a bad headache that won't go away, my vision is a little blurry, and my hands and face look puffy.

rows.message: 50M. For a few weeks I've had pain in my upper right belly that comes and goes, usually after a fatty meal. No fever, no yellowing of my skin or eyes.

rows.message: I have a small itchy red rash on my forearm since I did some gardening yesterday. It's not spreading and I'm breathing fine.

rows.message: 68F with COPD. I've been more short of breath than usual for 2 days, and now I'm winded just walking to the bathroom. My phlegm has turned green.
